en: The Questions of Milinda, Chapter on the Determination of Formless Phenomena: 12. The Question on the Ocean “Venerable sir, it has been said: ‘The ocean is deep, immeasurable, unfathomable. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is deep, immeasurable, unfathomable? “It is, great king, because of its depth, its breadth, and its vastness that the ocean is deep, immeasurable, unfathomable. “But how, venerable sir, is it through depth, breadth, and vastness that the ocean is deep, immeasurable, unfathomable? “The ocean, great king, gradually slopes away, gradually inclines, and gradually deepens; there is no abrupt precipice like that found in other bodies of water. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is deep through its depth. Furthermore, great king, the ocean is immeasurable in breadth. It extends for hundreds and thousands of leagues, and there is no measuring of its width. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is immeasurable in breadth. Furthermore, great king, the ocean is vast. It contains many hundreds and thousands of living beings, and there is no counting them. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is vast through its vastness. It is in these three ways, great king—through depth, breadth, and vastness—that the ocean is deep, immeasurable, unfathomable. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean does not mix with a corpse. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean does not mix with a corpse? “When a corpse, great king, enters the ocean, the ocean does not remain mixed with it. Rather, the current carries it to the shore, and there the waves cast it up onto dry land. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean does not mix with a corpse. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean does not tolerate a corpse. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean does not tolerate a corpse? “When a corpse, great king, enters the ocean, the ocean does not tolerate it. Rather, the current carries it to the shore, and there the waves cast it up onto dry land. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean does not tolerate a corpse. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is one flavor. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is one flavor? “Whatever water, great king, enters the ocean, all of it becomes the same salt flavor. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is one flavor. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean does not overflow its bounds. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean does not overflow its bounds? “Whatever rivers, great king, flow into the ocean, they do not cause it to overflow its bounds.

It is in this way, great king, that the ocean does not overflow its bounds. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is patient and enduring. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is patient and enduring? “Whatever rivers, great king, carry silt and mud into the ocean, the ocean remains patient and enduring. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is patient and enduring. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is the abode of great beings. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is the abode of great beings? “In the ocean, great king, there are these great beings: the Timi, the Timingala, the Timitimingala, the Asuras, the Nāgas, and the Gandhabbas. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is the abode of great beings. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is the source of great gems. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is the source of great gems? “In the ocean, great king, there are these great gems: pearls, gems, lapis lazuli, conch shells, quartz, coral, silver, gold, rubies, and cat’s-eye gems. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is the source of great gems. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is the source of great jewels. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is the source of great jewels? “In the ocean, great king, there are these great jewels: the jewel of the asuras, the jewel of the nāgas, and the jewel of the gandhabbas. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is the source of great jewels. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is the source of great treasures. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is the source of great treasures? “In the ocean, great king, there are these great treasures: the treasure of the asuras, the treasure of the nāgas, and the treasure of the gandhabbas. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is the source of great treasures. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is the source of great wealth. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is the source of great wealth? “In the ocean, great king, there are these great riches: pearls, gems, lapis lazuli, conch shells, quartz, coral, silver, gold, rubies, and cat’s-eye gems. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is the source of great wealth. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is the source of great prosperity. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is the source of great prosperity? “In the ocean, great king, there are these great prosperities: the prosperity of the asuras, the prosperity of the nāgas, and the prosperity of the gandhabbas. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is the source of great prosperity. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is the source of great power. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is the source of great power? “In the ocean, great king, there are these great powers: the power of the asuras, the power of the nāgas, and the power of the gandhabbas. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is the source of great power. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is the source of great majesty. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is the source of great majesty? “In the ocean, great king, there are these great majesties: the majesty of the asuras, the majesty of the nāgas, and the majesty of the gandhabbas. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is the source of great majesty. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is the source of great splendor. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is the source of great splendor? “In the ocean, great king, there are these great splendors: the splendor of the asuras, the splendor of the nāgas, and the splendor of the gandhabbas. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is the source of great splendor. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is the source of great glory. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is the source of great glory? “In the ocean, great king, there are these great glories: the glory of the asuras, the glory of the nāgas, and the glory of the gandhabbas. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is the source of great glory. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is the source of great renown. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is the source of great renown? “In the ocean, great king, there are these great renowns: the renown of the asuras, the renown of the nāgas, and the renown of the gandhabbas. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is the source of great renown. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is the source of great fame. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is the source of great fame? “In the ocean, great king, there are these great fames: the fame of the asuras, the fame of the nāgas, and the fame of the gandhabbas. It is in this way, great king, that the ocean is the source of great fame. “Venerable sir, it has also been said: ‘The ocean is the source of great light. How is it, venerable sir, that the ocean is the source of great light? “In the ocean, great king, there are these great lights: the light of the asuras, the light of the nāgas, and the light of the gandhabbas. "Venerable Nāgasena, it is said, 'the ocean, the ocean. For what reason is water called 'the ocean'?
“Great King, as much water as there is, so much salt is there;
as much salt as there is, so much water is there.
Thus ends the twelfth chapter, the Question on the Ocean.
